about: The same thing named in two languages or forms, and different things that look alike (memory_core 6.1.0, objects.py). Each persona is one end user's memory: its facts (subject, relation, object, family, the memory's words). Each new mention is asked alone against that memory. expected: the object of the memory it is the same thing as, or null. kind: same (must unite), false_friend (looks alike, must stay apart), different (related but another thing, must stay apart), ambiguous (reported apart, not scored), probe (the same written name in another context: the engine never asks it, because one written name is one object already; reported apart). Written by hand on 29 Oct 2026; no item comes from a bench the engine was tuned on. Extended on 30 Oct 2026 (the review of 6.1.0, P2.7): seven more personas without the filler, 138 hard negatives whose new sentence carries no disambiguator (class: exonym, a name that translates the stored one but names another place; homonym, a New-World place stored with its context against the Old World's name; company, a company and its parent, brand, product or division; part_of, a place and what contains it or is in it; near_name, names that look alike; against: the stored object it is built against) and 42 positives in another fact than the stored one (class not_paraphrase). The bench is data for measuring; no code reads it.
